summary: The blocking empty-backlog amendment is well placed (G0/feature start, G1/agent-owned MR create including Draft, G2/agent-owned merge), correctly separated from mid-feature `make mo-qc`, honest about UNKNOWN vs NOT-EMPTY, restrained about CI (no automatic YAML or branch-protection edits, `no_ci_surface` as a real outcome, `pull_request_target` refused as candidate proof), and it preserves every frozen decision with full U-/D-ledger traceability. Its external claims survive verification: gh 2.100.0, glab 1.117.0 and `orca skills list --json` behave exactly as §2.5/§4.6/§8.1 assert, and `§A-BACKLOG-01` is free in Git history. But I broke it in four concrete ways against this repository: (1) PASS requires a clean tree while `spec/` is untracked-and-unignored today, so G0/G1/G2 return UNKNOWN/dirty_worktree in Meta-O's own steady state and in any project that declines the §8.2 ignore proposal — and §3 explicitly permits other dirty user files, contradicting G0 outright; (2) §8.2's normative `git check-ignore --no-index` cannot distinguish a project-owned rule from a global excludesFile match, so it returns false PASS for exactly the case §8.2 forbids (verified: only `-v` reports provenance); (3) the MO-BACKLOG-* token/exit/reason contract is specified only 'в Meta-O' while B37, CI `covered` analysis and mo-setup verification all demand typed diagnostics from foreign-project implementations; (4) §14's mandated malformed/invalid-UTF-8 fixture roots fall inside markdownlint's `**/*.md` glob and `prettier --check .`, so they will redden `mo-qc`, and no slice mentions the ignore-config change. Additionally, CI `covered` is the largest new capability and the only contract in this spec without a named executing subject or outcome record schema, which reopens the very PROOF-BOUNDARY problem §14.1 was written to close.

blocking_findings.description: PASS requires a clean worktree and `UNKNOWN/dirty_worktree` blocks G0/G1/G2, but (a) 'clean' is never defined w.r.t. untracked vs tracked-modified, (b) Meta-O's own working artifacts make the tree dirty because `spec/` and `.orca/` are not covered by .gitignore, (c) §8.2 only *proposes* that ignore rule so a declining project is permanently blocked, (d) §3 explicitly preserves other dirty user files while G0 demands a clean tree, and (e) a CI job that installs dependencies before the gate dirties the tree for reasons unrelated to the backlog.
blocking_findings.evidence: Verified in /Users/alex/Develop/meta-o: `git status --porcelain` → `M docs/backlog.md`, `?? spec/2026-09-14-backlog-refinement-approval/`; `git check-ignore --no-index -- spec/` exits 1; .gitignore contains only node_modules, .DS_Store, dist/, __pycache__/, *.pyc. §8.3: 'доказанно пустой, но dirty tree даёт UNKNOWN/dirty_worktree, не PASS'. §3: 'другие пользовательские dirty files не затрагиваются'.
blocking_findings.required_change: Define tree state precisely and decouple it from unrelated dirt: judge the candidate from the committed object (e.g. `git cat-file blob HEAD:<declared-path>` after `git rev-parse HEAD`, re-read HEAD after) so the gate proves the candidate's emptiness regardless of working-tree state; reserve `dirty_worktree` for divergence on the declared backlog path itself and report unrelated dirt as an informational field. State explicitly whether §8.2 ignore coverage is a precondition of G1/G2, and resolve the §3-vs-G0 contradiction in one direction.

blocking_findings.description: The normative probe `git check-ignore --no-index -- <path>` exits 0 for a match originating in core.excludesFile or .git/info/exclude, which §8.2 explicitly refuses to accept as a substitute for a project-owned rule. The named command therefore cannot prove the requirement it states, and yields a false PASS on a developer machine with global excludes while a fresh checkout has no posture at all.
blocking_findings.evidence: Verified: `git check-ignore -v --no-index -- node_modules/` prints `.gitignore:5:node_modules\tnode_modules/` (source visible only with -v); the bare form prints nothing and exits 0 regardless of which ignore file matched. §8.2: 'Глобальный exclude, user-level ignore и изменение tracked state не используются как замена project-owned правилу'.
blocking_findings.required_change: Make the probe `git check-ignore -v --no-index -- <path>` per path and require the reported source file to be a repository-tracked ignore file (verifiable with `git ls-files --error-unmatch <source>`); a match sourced from a global or .git/info/exclude file is a setup gap, not coverage. Update B35 accordingly.

blocking_findings.description: The MO-BACKLOG-EMPTY/NOT-EMPTY/UNKNOWN header grammar, closed reason enum, stdout/stderr split and nonzero rule are normative only for Meta-O. For other projects mo-setup merely 'предлагает project-specific реализацию в языке и task runner проекта' with no required output contract, yet the named consumers — the project-contract-bound agent at G1/G2, B37's 'typed diagnostic', mo-setup's verification of non-mutating behaviour, and CI `covered` analysis of the 'exact closure command' — all presuppose one. Outside Meta-O the NOT-EMPTY vs UNKNOWN distinction (the core of 'do not mistake an unreadable backlog for an empty one') silently degrades to 'nonzero'.
blocking_findings.evidence: §8.3: 'В Meta-O её публичное имя: make mo-backlog-empty' followed by the token/enum contract; then 'В другом проекте mo-setup ... предлагает project-specific реализацию в языке и task runner проекта и фиксирует выбранные path/command'. B37 requires the agent to show a typed diagnostic with no statement of where a foreign project's typed diagnostic comes from.
blocking_findings.required_change: Declare the header grammar, reason enum and nonzero rule as a named, versioned portable contract that any project-owned implementation must satisfy (language- and runner-agnostic), and have mo-setup verify it by running the declared command against a disposable fixture copy; or explicitly downgrade foreign-project consumers to 'nonzero blocks' and remove typed-diagnostic expectations from B37 and from CI coverage criteria.

blocking_findings.description: CI coverage analysis is the largest new capability in the amendment (active-entrypoint resolution via authenticated metadata, static include/reusable-workflow graph resolution, rules/if/only/except and path-filter coverage of three change classes, shell exit-masking detection, skipped-prerequisite detection, required-status policy read) yet it is the only contract in this spec with no named executing subject, no outcome record schema, no bounded algorithm and no named parser. §14.1 was written precisely to forbid this for the Issue table; the same discipline is not applied here, so slice 11's 'GitHub/GitLab CI fixtures' have no stated consumer.
blocking_findings.evidence: §14.1 names the subject of each of three proof layers for §4.5; §8.3's CI section names outcomes (covered/config_present/no_ci_surface/unknown) and criteria but no subject; §15 slice 11 lists 'GitHub/GitLab CI fixtures' among deterministic tests without saying what code they exercise; §4.5 mandates a bounded record with fixed fields for Issue dispositions, while CI discovery gets none.
blocking_findings.required_change: Apply the §14.1 three-layer structure to CI discovery: name the subject of each layer (agent reasoning vs a test-only evaluator in tests/), define a bounded outcome record with fixed fields (provider, entrypoint, resolved graph status, job/step identity, event coverage, required-policy status, outcome, unresolved items), name the YAML parser (js-yaml is already a project dependency), and reduce `covered` to a cheap provable core with all subtler heuristics able only to downgrade to `unknown`.

blocking_findings.description: §14 requires fixture roots covering missing, unreadable, invalid-UTF-8 and malformed-schema backlog files, but markdownlint-cli2 globs `**/*.md` and prettier checks `.` with ignores that do not include tests/fixtures. Deliberately malformed or invalid-UTF-8 Markdown fixtures will make `mo-lint` — and therefore `make mo-qc` — fail, which contradicts §14's own promise that QC stays green with the fixtures present. No slice mentions updating .prettierignore or .markdownlint-cli2.jsonc.
blocking_findings.evidence: Makefile mo-lint runs `npx markdownlint-cli2` and `npx prettier --check .`; .markdownlint-cli2.jsonc globs `**/*.md` and ignores only node_modules/, skills/, spec/, docs/references/, docs/research/, shared/licenses/; .prettierignore ignores skills/, node_modules/, dist/, templates/, spec/, docs/references/, docs/research/. tests/fixtures/ currently holds only .mjs. §14: 'make mo-qc с valid non-empty fixture остаётся зелёным' — the malformed cases are not considered.
blocking_findings.required_change: Name the lint-configuration change (extend .prettierignore and markdownlint ignores to the fixture root, or hold fixtures outside the *.md lint surface) in the slice that adds the fixtures, and extend the acceptance assertion to 'mo-qc stays green with the complete fixture set present', not only the valid one.

blocking_findings.description: PASS requires zero `###` entries AND no other substantive content under `## Открыто`. A section containing prose but no headings must therefore fail, and the only available token is `MO-BACKLOG-NOT-EMPTY ... entries=0`, whose count field is indistinguishable from the PASS signature. A machine consumer keying on `entries=` sees a contradiction, and the spec presents these fields as the machine-readable contract.
blocking_findings.evidence: §8.3: 'canonical ## Открыто содержит ноль ### entries и иной substantive content' and the three header grammars, where PASS ends `entries=0` and NOT-EMPTY ends `entries=<n>`.
blocking_findings.required_change: Disambiguate: either route prose-only failure to `MO-BACKLOG-UNKNOWN reason=schema_invalid`, or add a distinct field/token for substantive non-entry content so `entries=0` never appears on a failing line.

blocking_findings.description: The closed reason enum has no code for 'not a Git repository', 'declared command or task-runner target absent/unexecutable', or 'declared backlog path is a directory/symlink outside the repository', all of which are reachable states for a gate that must run in foreign projects and CI checkouts. Folding them into git_head_unreadable or internal_error loses the diagnostic value the enum exists to provide.
blocking_findings.evidence: §8.3 enum: path_undeclared, path_ambiguous, missing_file, not_regular_file, unreadable_file, invalid_utf8, schema_invalid, git_head_unreadable, dirty_worktree, head_changed, internal_error.
blocking_findings.required_change: Extend the closed enum with codes for non-repository context and absent/unexecutable declared command, and state which code covers a path resolving outside the repository root.

non_blocking_findings.description: Meta-O's only remote is github.com and the repository has no CI configuration at all, so discovery yields no_ci_surface and setup will not propose creating CI unasked. In the project that ships the requirement, nothing but agent instructions enforces G1/G2 and a human merge is entirely unchecked. This should be stated as a known limitation with a next step rather than left implicit.
non_blocking_findings.evidence: `git remote -v` → origin https://github.com/shkarupa-alex/meta-o.git; no .github/ and no .gitlab-ci.yml present; §8.3: 'если CI действительно отсутствует/выключен, no_ci_surface фиксирует gap, но setup не предлагает создавать CI-инфраструктуру с нуля без отдельного запроса'.
non_blocking_findings.required_change: State the self-hosting limitation explicitly in §8.3 or §17 with its practical impact and next step.

non_blocking_findings.description: B39 requires mo-setup to classify GitLab CI coverage against authenticated read-only project metadata and merge-train reachability, but no GitLab target is available to this project and the spec never names where the E2E actor/target comes from. B39 risks being permanently 'unknown', leaving the GitLab half of U-19 unproven.
non_blocking_findings.evidence: Only remote is github.com; B39 requires active custom entrypoint and MR/merge-train reachability checks.
non_blocking_findings.required_change: Name the E2E target provisioning for B39 (disposable fixture project, an existing GitLab project, or recorded-surface fixtures), or declare it conditional with an explicit not-available outcome analogous to §13's desired-profile policy.

non_blocking_findings.description: The slices omit the mechanical repository work the new checker requires: a new .PHONY Make target, new `node --check tools/<module>.mjs` lines in mo-lint (which enumerates tools by filename), a purpose docblock naming §A-BACKLOG-01 (enforced by tests/eslint-symbol-purpose.test.mjs and the CLAUDE.md purpose contract), and the CLAUDE.md-mandated commit-message proof that a mature tool or configuration cannot solve the check. Slice 6 also bundles five unrelated contracts, of which CI inspection alone is the largest new capability.
non_blocking_findings.evidence: Makefile mo-lint lists each tools/*.mjs explicitly; CLAUDE.md: 'A custom checker needs proof in its commit message that a plugin or configuration cannot solve it'; §15 slice 2 mentions only 'комментарии Makefile'.
non_blocking_findings.required_change: Enumerate the Makefile/lint/purpose-comment/commit-message obligations in the relevant slice, and split CI inspection into its own slice with its own evidence.

non_blocking_findings.description: D-20 (external workflow engine/state store) is rejected in §2a but absent from §16's rejected list, where every other rejection is restated; and §16's D-19 line names only the test-only table evaluator as an authorized exception, while D-48 authorizes a second one (the project-owned backlog checker), so the exception surface cannot be read off §16 alone.
non_blocking_findings.evidence: §16 lists 'новый orchestration/report/Issue helper или registry в поставке — rejected; test-only table evaluator ... allowed'; D-48 authorizes the narrow runtime checker; §2a approach C rejects the state store.
non_blocking_findings.required_change: Add the workflow-engine/state-store rejection to §16 and name both authorized executable exceptions on the D-19 line.

non_blocking_findings.description: The 'exactly one ASCII header line on stderr' property belongs to the checker, but consumers invoking the public Make target also see `make: *** [mo-backlog-empty] Error N` on the same channel. The spec presents stderr as the typed channel without stating that callers must locate the token rather than assume a single line.
non_blocking_findings.evidence: §8.3: 'checker до detail печатает ровно одну ASCII header line: PASS — в stdout, любой отказ — в stderr'; GNU Make emits its own failure line to stderr and exits 2.
non_blocking_findings.required_change: State that consumers match the MO-BACKLOG-* token anywhere in the stream and must tolerate task-runner noise on the same channel.

assumptions: I reviewed only the repository state at the current working tree and the spec text supplied; I did not open other spec/** council artifacts, per the task constraint.

I read the verified-surface claims (§2.5, §4.6, §8.1) as in-scope for spot verification because the spec asserts them as facts about installed tools; I confirmed a representative subset rather than every flag.

I assumed 'tree clean' in §8.3 was intended to include untracked files, since the spec offers no narrower definition and the UNKNOWN reason is named dirty_worktree; if a narrower meaning was intended, BLG-GATE-DIRTY-TREE-CONFLATION still stands because the meaning is unstated.

I assumed fixture roots for the malformed/invalid-UTF-8 cases would live inside the repository (e.g. tests/fixtures/) rather than be generated into a temp directory at test time; if generated at runtime, BLG-FIXTURES-BREAK-MO-LINT reduces to a clarification request.

I treated 'project-specific реализация' in a foreign project as producing an executable the agent and CI invoke directly, since B37 and CI coverage both depend on invoking the declared closure command.
